items.title: Miami-Dade deputies accuse 4 of $100K Bath & Body Works cargo theft, candle resale scheme

headlines: FOUR ARRESTED IN 100K MIAMI DADE CANDLE THEFT SCHEME
MASSIVE MIAMI SCENTED CANDLE RING BUSTED
HOW AN AUDIT UNRAVELED A 100K MIAMI CANDLE HEIST
draft.article:
Four South Florida residents were arrested Thursday after an internal audit uncovered more than $100,000 in stolen Bath and Body Works merchandise from the London Square shopping center near Miami Executive Airport.

Deputies say delivery driver Michel Sanchez-Escanelle, 44, of Hialeah, diverted cartons during trips from a Medley warehouse, passing boxes to Lecsi Linet Figueroa-Martinez, 24. Stolen goods were stored at the northwest Miami-Dade home of Yosdany Martinez-Bravo, 49.

Pembroke Pines resident Marlie Rodriguez-Benavides, 35, admitted to buying the 25-dollar retail candles for 8 dollars each to resell for 10 dollars. Investigators seized 17 cartons and about 140,000 dollars in cash. All four suspects face felony charges.

items.title: Miami-Dade district could close 5 more schools. Here's the list

headlines: MIAMI-DADE SCHOOL DISTRICT TARGETS SIX SCHOOLS FOR CLOSURE PROCESS
MORE MIAMI-DADE SCHOOL CLOSURES COULD BE COMING
WHAT ENROLLMENT DROPS MEAN FOR OUR MIAMI-DADE SCHOOLS
draft.article:
Miami-Dade County Public Schools has restarted a review that could close several local campuses. According to Superintendent Rafael Villalobos, the Attendance Boundary Committee classified six schools as targeted, with five facing consolidation and one slated for conversion next school year. Another 28 area schools are listed as advised for probable boundary changes.

The move follows significant enrollment drops across Miami-Dade. On August 13, opening day enrollment for traditional public schools dropped to 215,078, down from 230,172 the previous year. District media relations director Elmo Lugo noted that district-operated schools landed 5,333 students below projections. Villalobos previously paused reviews in September to reassess selections before resuming work this fall.

items.title: Plea deal rejected for assistant principal accused of killing Miami-Dade teacher
items.desc: A judge rejected the plea agreement Ernest Roberts was accepting for the killing of Kameela Russell, a beloved teacher at Norland High.

headlines: JUDGE REJECTS PLEA DEAL IN NORLAND TEACHER MURDER CASE
NO PLEA DEAL FOR MIAMI ASSISTANT PRINCIPAL
NORLAND HIGH MURDER CASE HEADS TO TRIAL AFTER REJECTION
draft.article:
A Miami-Dade judge rejected a plea deal on Friday for former Norland High assistant principal Ernest Joseph Roberts, sending the 47-year-old to trial for the 2019 killing of North Miami-Dade teacher Kameela Russell.

Russell, 41, vanished in May 2019 after failing to pick up her daughter in Miami Gardens, and her body was later discovered in a canal. Roberts had agreed to plead guilty to second-degree murder in exchange for 30 years in prison followed by five years of probation, reduced from a first-degree murder indictment.

Circuit Judge Alberto Milian denied the agreement following emotional statements from Russell's family. Milian then recused himself, sending the case to a new judge for trial.

Kilongo was hit with a fourth lawsuit in September, filed by painter Yirui Jia in the Supreme Court of the State of New York. Jia, who presented a solo exhibition at Jupiter in Miami Beach in 2025, represents the third artist claiming Kilongo withheld proceeds from art sales. According to the legal filing, Kilongo allegedly paid Jia just $2,000 out of $42,000 owed for the sales of five of her paintings.

headlines: FORMER DOLPHINS CORNERBACK KADER KOHOU SIGNS WITH BUFFALO BILLS
EX-DOLPHINS STARTER HEADS TO DIVISION RIVAL
FORMER SOUTH FLORIDA STANDOUT CORNERBACK JOINS FAMILIAR DIVISION ENEMY
draft.article:
Former Miami Dolphins starting cornerback Kader Kohou has signed a practice squad contract with the Buffalo Bills. Kohou recently became available after his release from the Kansas City Chiefs practice squad following a November 1 game against Denver.

Kohou first arrived in South Florida in 2022 as an undrafted rookie out of East Texas A&M before earning a major role in the secondary. Over three seasons with Miami, the 5-foot-10 defensive back started 38 of 47 games, recording 25 pass breakups and three interceptions. His first career start was a memorable 21-19 victory over Buffalo at Hard Rock Stadium in September 2022.

After spending 2025 on injured reserve, Kohou now joins Miami's AFC East rival.
